dedupe_keys.name: hot disaster response mapping and building damage datasets on hdx

description: Besides its country export grid, the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team publishes about 30 event and campaign datasets on HDX (count on 2026-09-26) with buildings, roads and facilities mapped during disaster activations, crowdsourced and AI-assisted building damage assessments, and mapathon outputs. The Nepal flood 2026 fAIr assessment scores 8,421 OpenStreetMap buildings in the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi corridor as no visible, minor, major damage or destroyed, with a confidence value, validated against 3,896 manually tagged buildings (destroyed precision 0.91, recall 0.78). A Myanmar pilot with local mappers tagged damaged buildings in 20 townships after the March 2025 earthquake using MapSwipe, Tasking Manager and MapRoulette. The Türkiye export holds buildings tagged destroyed after the 6 February 2023 earthquake, and the Venezuela M7.5 set gives grid areas where AI-detected damage was confirmed by majority MapSwipe votes. Event exports cover the August 2026 Colombia earthquake, the January 2026 Mozambique floods, Cyclone Gezani in Madagascar and the 2026 DRC and Uganda Ebola outbreak; the LATAM Regional Mapatón 2026 sets hold footprints mapped from 13 June to 31 July 2026 in risk-priority areas of eight countries. Access: GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage and KML files, some with post-event imagery. Licence: mostly ODbL; the mapatón sets are CC BY and the Venezuela set cites CC BY-NC-SA fAIr detections. Caveats: AI calls can be inflated by cross-sensor imagery and cloud, crowdsourced tags are incomplete, and field verification is the ground truth. Simulation uses are observed damage for validating fragility and loss models, and exposure layers for response planning. Related records: HOT country exports on HDX and UNOSAT damage assessments.
licence: ODbL-1.0 for most sets; CC-BY-4.0 for the mapathon sets; other terms per dataset
